name: H-33
label: forming
assay_method: S1 nuclease sensitivity assay (single-strand-specific nuclease probing of the plasmid; 'as described [17]', i.e. the S1/P1 nuclease sensitivity assay of Wang & Vasquez 2004 PNAS). Downstream readouts in the same paper: anti-8-oxodG immuno-slot blot, qPCR damage assay, supF mutagenesis in COS-7 cells.
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled 2,100-bp plasmid carrying the 33-bp H-DNA-forming c-MYC sequence (constructed from the 5,100-bp parent pMycY); plasmid prepared in E. coli by alkaline lysis / QIAGEN Maxi Kit
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling (supercoiled plasmid DNA); no sigma value reported
source: PMID 39950343 (PMC11826088), Materials and methods, 'Construction and preparation of substrates for the immuno-slot blot assay', plus Results (Supplementary Fig. S2). The pH value is not restated there and is taken from the method paper it cites, PMID 15342911 (Wang & Vasquez 2004 PNAS 101:13448, PMC518777), Materials and Methods 'Analysis of H-DNA Conformations in the Modified Plasmids' and Fig. 1B legend.
evidence_quote: "the formation of H-DNA was verified using an S1 nuclease assay as described [17]" (PMID 39950343); "Plasmids were digested with S1 nuclease at pH 4.5 (Upper) or P1 nuclease at pH 7.1 (Lower)" (PMID 15342911)
notes: Assay identity, DNA context and supercoiling are explicit in PMID 39950343; the buffer pH (4.5) and the paired P1-at-pH-7.1 control come only from the primary method paper it cites (Wang & Vasquez 2004 PNAS, PMID 15342911), which used the same parent plasmids (pMycY/pcMyc). Temperature and salt are reported in neither. In Wang & Vasquez 2004 the equivalent pcMyc insert was S1-sensitive at pH 4.5 AND P1-sensitive at pH 7.1, so H-DNA formed at both acidic and neutral pH for this c-MYC sequence. Record sequence is 30 bp; the paper's H-33 is 33 bp (5'-AATTCGCGGGAGGGGCGCTTATGGGGAGGGAAC). Separate, unrelated conditions in the same paper: Fenton oxidation of the supercoiled plasmid in 30 mM sodium acetate (pH 5.2), 25 mM NaCl, 4 mM MgCl2, 30 min at room temperature; and model oligonucleotide triplexes annealed in 20 mM sodium cacodylate pH 7.0, 100 mM NaCl, 0.1 mM EDTA, 10 mM MgCl2 for CD/thermal analysis. Supplementary Fig. S2 (the actual S1 gel) was not retrieved.

name: B-33
label: non_forming
assay_method: S1 nuclease sensitivity assay (same assay as the H-33 substrate, run as the matched control; 'as described [17]')
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled 2,100-bp plasmid carrying the 33-bp control B-DNA sequence (constructed from the 5,100-bp parent pMycAG); plasmid prepared in E. coli by alkaline lysis / QIAGEN Maxi Kit
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling (supercoiled plasmid DNA); no sigma value reported
source: PMID 39950343 (PMC11826088), Fig. 1B legend, Materials and methods and Results. Non-formation of H-DNA by the identical pMycAG-derived control under the S1 assay is shown directly in the cited method paper, PMID 15342911 (Wang & Vasquez 2004 PNAS, PMC518777), Results and Fig. 1B.
evidence_quote: "B-33 is the 33-bp control B-DNA sequence that has two base substitutions that disrupt the mirror symmetry to prevent H-DNA formation [17]" (PMID 39950343); "nor from the mutated c-myc control plasmid, pMycAG" (PMID 15342911, S1 assay at pH 4.5)
notes: B-33 is the matched non-forming control: same length and GC content as H-33, two base substitutions destroying the mirror repeat. PMID 39950343 states only that H-DNA was confirmed in the H-33 substrates (Supplementary Fig. S2) and does not restate the B-33 S1 result; the explicit absence of S1 cleavage for the parent pMycAG control, at pH 4.5, is in PMID 15342911. pH/temperature/salt as for HDNA0027. Record sequence is 30 bp; the paper's B-33 is 33 bp (5'-AATTCGCGGGAGGGGCGCTTATGGAGGGGGAAC).

name: GA32
label: forming
assay_method: in vivo plasmid-plasmid homologous recombination assay in cultured human cells (G418-resistant colony counts), with Kpn I-induced double-strand breaks as the supercoiling-dependence control. NO direct structural assay (no S1 nuclease, no chemical probing) is performed in this paper; the H-form transition is cited from Mirkin 1987 Nature 330:495-497.
assay_dna_context: closed-circular, cesium chloride-purified supercoiled pSV2neo-derived plasmids (pDLGA / pDRGA) transfected into human EJ bladder carcinoma cells
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported (calcium phosphate-mediated transfection; cells maintained in DMEM/10% fetal calf serum)
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling (closed-circular supercoiled plasmid); introducing double-strand breaks with Kpn I relaxed the supercoils and abolished the stimulation
source: PMID 7892237 (PMC42439), Materials and Methods ('Constructs', 'Tissue Culture and Transfections'), Results ('Double-Strand Breaks Negate the Triplex-Induced Stimulation') and Fig. 2 legend
evidence_quote: "Throughout this study, cesium chloride-purified, and thus closed-circular supercoiled, plasmid DNA was used."
notes: The earlier curation hint 'S1 / recombination' is wrong for this paper: Rooney & Moore 1995 contains no S1 nuclease or chemical probing data. Only the recombination phenotype (3- to 5-fold stimulation, abolished by double-strand breaks) is measured, and no pH, temperature or buffer/salt conditions for structure formation are given. The paper explicitly says GA32 forms H-DNA with difficulty - "when X=A and Y=G (AG32) or X=G and Y=A (GA32), the transition is much more difficult" - and attributes GA32's recombinogenic effect to the *H-DNA (pyrimidine.purine.purine) form, whose formation "has not been shown directly but was inferred from basic principles". The primary structural study for the XY32 series is Mirkin 1987 Nature 330:495-497 (superhelix-induced, pH-dependent transition), which was not accessible and was not read. Independent S1/P1 data for the same GA32 sequence exist in PMID 15342911 (S1-sensitive at pH 4.5 but weakly, no signal at pH 7.1) if the curator wants a structural condition.

name: AA32
label: forming
assay_method: in vivo plasmid-plasmid homologous recombination assay in cultured human cells (G418-resistant colony counts), with Kpn I-induced double-strand breaks as the supercoiling-dependence control. NO direct structural assay in this paper; the superhelix-induced, pH-dependent H-form transition of AA32 is cited from Mirkin 1987 Nature 330:495-497.
assay_dna_context: closed-circular, cesium chloride-purified supercoiled pSV2neo-derived plasmids (pDLAA / pDRAA) transfected into human EJ bladder carcinoma cells
assay_ph: not reported (stated only to be 'pH-dependent')
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported (calcium phosphate-mediated transfection; cells maintained in DMEM/10% fetal calf serum)
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling (closed-circular supercoiled plasmid); introducing double-strand breaks with Kpn I relaxed the supercoils and abolished the stimulation
source: PMID 7892237 (PMC42439), Introduction, Materials and Methods ('Constructs', 'Tissue Culture and Transfections') and Results
evidence_quote: "has been shown to undergo a superhelix-induced, pH-dependent structural transition to intramolecular H-DNA when X=Y=A or X=Y=G, named AA32 and GG32, respectively"
notes: Same caveat as HDNA0055: no S1 nuclease or chemical probing in this paper, and no numeric pH, temperature or ionic conditions anywhere in it. AA32 is the sequence for which H-DNA formation is best supported, but only by citation to Mirkin 1987 Nature 330:495-497 (not read; paywalled). The paper's own measurement is a 3- to 5-fold stimulation of homologous recombination that requires negative supercoiling.

name: cMYC_NHE
label: forming
assay_method: chemical probing of a supercoiled plasmid with dimethyl sulfate (DMS), diethyl pyrocarbonate (DEPC) and osmium tetroxide (OsO4), read out by piperidine cleavage and end-labelled sequencing gels; plus an oligonucleotide-association (gel mobility) assay
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled plasmid subclone pc-myc282 (human c-myc Pvu II -353 bp to Sma I -101 bp inserted at the Hinc II site of pUC13); 10 ug per probing reaction, 2 ug per oligonucleotide-association reaction
assay_ph: 4.0-5.0 for the H-DNA pattern (probing was done at pH 4, 5, 6 and 7; the H-DNA reactivities were present at pH 4 and 5 and absent at pH 6-7). Oligonucleotide-association assay at pH 4.0
assay_temperature: 22 °C for chemical probing (DMS 2 min, OsO4 5 min, DEPC 20 min); 45 °C for 20 min for the oligonucleotide-association assay, with electrophoresis at 50 V for 20 h
assay_ionic_conditions: 50 mM Na acetate (pH 4 or 5) or 100 mM Na cacodylate (pH 6 or 7), 100 ul reactions; OsO4 reactions made 10 mM in OsO4 and started with 2 ul pyridine. No added NaCl or MgCl2 reported. Oligonucleotide-association assay: 100 mM Na acetate pH 4.0, run in 10 mM Na acetate pH 4.0 agarose gel buffer
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling (superhelical plasmid purified from E. coli by the Holmes and Quigley method); no sigma value reported
source: PMID 2678005, Materials and Methods ('Plasmid preparation, chemical modification, and gel electrophoresis'; 'Oligonucleotide-Association assay'), Results ('Chemical probing for H-DNA structures') and Fig. 2/Fig. 3 legends
evidence_quote: "50mM Na acetate at pH 4 or 5 and 100 mM Na cacadylate at pH 6 or 7 were utilized. ... The samples were vortexed and DMS samples were incubated 2' at 22°C." (OCR of the scanned PDF; 'cacadylate' = cacodylate)
notes: H-DNA signature was pH-dependent: "At acidic pH (4 and 5) three thymines on the pyrimidine-rich strand show hyper-reactivity with OsO4" and, for DEPC, "The hyper-reactivity of these bases is not observed at pH 6.0"; DMS hypo-reactivity of eight guanines (Hoogsteen protection) was seen at pH 4 and 5. So pH 4-5 plus native negative supercoiling is the H-DNA-forming condition; pH 6-7 gave the B-DNA pattern. The record gives no sequence (c-MYC NHE III1 / nuclease-sensitive element). Text was obtained by pdftotext from the scanned PMC PDF (PMC334884), so verbatim quotes carry OCR artifacts. Note the paper has a published erratum (Nucleic Acids Res 1989 Oct 25;17(20):8412), which was not retrieved.

name: cMYC_NSE (ACCCTCCCC)4
label: forming
assay_method: not reported (abstract states only that mutant NSEs were "examined for transcriptional activity and for intra- and intermolecular triplex forming ability"; the specific assays and their conditions are in the paywalled full text)
assay_dna_context: not reported
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: not reported
source: PMID 8161210, abstract
evidence_quote: "The NSE was mutated and examined for transcriptional activity and for intra- and intermolecular triplex forming ability. The transcriptional activity of mutant NSEs can be predicted by the element's ability to form H-DNA and not by repeat number, position, or the number of mutant base pairs."
notes: Unresolved. No open-access copy: no PMC record, and jbc-style/Elsevier routes (doi.org/10.1006/abbi.1994.1162 and sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0003986184711623) returned HTTP 403, so the Methods were never read. The abstract contains no assay conditions at all, and the earlier hint 'S1' could not be confirmed from any source actually read. If a curator needs a stand-in condition for the same c-myc NSE element, the same group's PMID 2678005 (Kinniburgh 1989 NAR, curated here as HDNA0057) probed the NSE in a supercoiled plasmid at pH 4-5, 22 °C, 50 mM Na acetate - but that is a different construct (genomic NSE, not the synthetic (ACCCTCCCC)4 repeat) and must not be copied into this record without reading the 1994 paper.

name: BCL6_ClusterII_Pu
label: forming
assay_method: triplex gel-shift assay (radiolabelled purine-rich oligomer VG10 titrated with complementary pyrimidine-rich oligomers VG11 or VG12, resolved on 15% native PAGE) plus circular dichroism spectroscopy; single-strandedness of the region in cells was assessed separately by a sodium bisulfite modification assay
assay_dna_context: oligonucleotides (synthetic VG10 purine-rich oligomer from the BCL6 cluster II breakpoint region annealed with VG11 or VG12; 0.1-500 nM titration for the gel shift, 3-4 uM for CD). The separate bisulfite assay used genomic DNA from SUDHL8 cells extracted under non-denaturing conditions
assay_ph: 8.0 (triplex gel-shift and CD, Tris-borate-MgCl2 buffer). Sodium bisulfite modification assay: 2.5 M sodium bisulfite, pH 5.2
assay_temperature: 37 °C overnight for triplex formation, with native gels run at 150 V at 4 °C; CD samples incubated 15 min-1 h at 37 °C and spectra recorded at 25 °C / room temperature. Bisulfite assay: 16 h at 37 °C in the dark
assay_ionic_conditions: 90 mM Tris, 90 mM borate, 10 mM MgCl2 (pH 8.0) ('TBM' buffer) for both the gel shift and the CD; no monovalent salt added
assay_supercoiling: linear (none) - the triplex was assayed on free oligonucleotides, not on supercoiled DNA; not reported for the genomic bisulfite assay
source: PMID 38196006 (PMC11072719), Materials and methods, 'Analysis of triplex DNA', 'Electrophoretic mobility shift assay', 'Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy' and 'Sodium bisulfite modification assay'; Results, 'Formation of triple-helical DNA structure at BCL6 cluster II region' and Fig. 6 legend
evidence_quote: "evaluated for the formation of triplex DNA in 90 mM Tris, 90 mM Borate and 10 mM MgCl 2 (pH 8.0) at 37 °C overnight. The products were then resolved on 15% native polyacrylamide gels at 150 V at 4 °C"
notes: The earlier hint 'bisulfite / antibody' is only partly right: there is no antibody assay for the triplex. Triplex evidence is a gel shift plus a CD peak shift (260 nm to 270-275 nm; Fig. 6E legend reports 280-290 nm), using VG10 annealed to a separate complementary strand that then folds back by Hoogsteen bonding - so the demonstration is on oligonucleotides at neutral-to-alkaline pH with 10 mM Mg2+, not on supercoiled plasmid and not at acidic pH, even though the abstract describes the product as "intramolecular ... triplex DNA". The sodium bisulfite assay (genomic DNA in SUDHL8 cells, pH 5.2, 16 h at 37 °C) was used for single-strandedness at the hairpin/cruciform region, not specifically for the triplex. Record gives no sequence (BCL6 5'UTR cluster II purine tract).

name: FXN_GAA10
label: forming
assay_method: 2D agarose gel electrophoresis of topoisomers; chemical probing (chloroacetaldehyde, KMnO4, and DMS-protection) read out by radiolabeled primer extension; atomic force microscopy
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled pUC8 plasmid; pGAA9 carries (GAA)9*(TTC)9 with FRDA genomic AT-rich flanks, control pGAA9NF carries the pure (GAA)9*(TTC)9 tract with no flanks
assay_ph: pH 7.6 chemical-probing buffer (0.5x TEN); results reported as formation 'at pH 7.4' / neutral pH; 2D gels run in TAE pH 8.3
assay_temperature: 37 C (chemical probing, and first dimension of the 2D gel); AFM samples deposited at 20 C
assay_ionic_conditions: 0.5x TEN buffer (5 mM Tris-HCl, 25 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, pH 7.6), with or without 2 mM MgCl2 added
assay_supercoiling: resolved topoisomer fractions spanning average superhelical densities sigma = 0 to sigma = -0.09; Figure 3 lanes are sigma = -0.046 and sigma = -0.088
source: PMID 14978261 (PMC373408), Materials and Methods sections 'Plasmids', 'Two-dimensional agarose gel electrophoresis', 'Chemical probe analysis', 'AFM imaging', plus Figure 3 legend and Results
evidence_quote: in 40 ul of 0.5x TEN buffer (5 mM Tris-HCl, 25 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM EDTA, pH 7.6) or 0.5x TEN buffer appended with 2 mM MgCl 2 were probed with 0.5% chloroacetaldehyde (CAA) for 8 min and 1 mM KMnO 4 for 5 min at 37 degrees C.
notes: Record is a synthetic pure (GAA)10 tract matched only at class/length level; the study tested n = 9, 23 and 42 cloned with FRDA genomic flanks. Directly relevant caveat for a pure tract: the no-flank control pGAA9NF needed far more negative supercoiling, with CAA reactivity only at sigma >= -0.09, so the very stable H-DNA at pH 7.4 depended on T*A*T triads contributed by the AT-rich flanks. Multiple conditions tested (eight topoisomer fractions, +/- 2 mM MgCl2).

name: FXN_GAA33
label: forming
assay_method: 2D agarose gel electrophoresis of topoisomers; chemical probing (chloroacetaldehyde, KMnO4, and DMS-protection) read out by radiolabeled primer extension; atomic force microscopy
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled pUC8 plasmid; pGAA23 and pGAA42 carry (GAA)23 and interrupted 42-unit (GAA) repeats flanked by FRDA genomic sequence
assay_ph: pH 7.6 chemical-probing buffer (0.5x TEN); results reported as formation 'at pH 7.4' / neutral pH; 2D gels run in TAE pH 8.3

source: PMID 14978261 (PMC373408), Materials and Methods sections 'Plasmids', 'Two-dimensional agarose gel electrophoresis', 'Chemical probe analysis', plus Figure 5 legend and Results

notes: Record is a synthetic pure (GAA)33 tract with no exactly matching construct: length 33 falls between the study's pGAA23 and pGAA42, so this is a class-level match only. At n = 42 and higher negative supercoiling a single H-DNA became less favorable and the data fit a bi-triplex instead, so the 'prefer the condition under which H-DNA was demonstrated' choice is the intermediate superhelicity regime. Multiple conditions tested.

name: FXN_GAA66
label: forming
assay_method: formation of 'sticky DNA' by self-association of two purine*purine*pyrimidine (R*R*Y) triplexes in plasmids; the individual techniques are not named in the abstract and the full text could not be read
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled plasmid
assay_ph: neutral pH (no numeric value given in the abstract)
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling of plasmids
source: PMID 10230399, abstract
evidence_quote: Sticky DNA is formed by the association of two purine.purine.pyrimidine (R.R.Y) triplexes in negatively supercoiled plasmids at neutral pH.
notes: Full text is not in PMC and the publisher blocked retrieval (HTTP 403 from ScienceDirect), so pH, temperature and ionic details in the Experimental Procedures were not read and are left as reported/not reported from the abstract alone. The record length (GAA)66 is consistent with the study's threshold: '> 59 repeats' were needed to adopt the sticky conformation. Caveat on structure class: sticky DNA is a dimeric R*R*Y (purine-motif) triplex, not the classic intramolecular Py*Pu*Py H-DNA, so the match to an H-DNA benchmark is approximate.

name: CANVAS_AAGGG10
label: forming
assay_method: chemical probing with potassium permanganate (KMnO4) read out as primer-extension termination (Thermo Sequenase); supported by orientation-dependent in vitro DNA polymerization stalling (Thermo Sequenase, Vent exo-, T7) and 2D gel electrophoresis of replication intermediates in yeast and human cells
assay_dna_context: negatively supercoiled plasmid pJH2 carrying (A2G3)10 = (AAGGG)10, with pJH9 carrying nonpathogenic (A4G)10 as the control
assay_ph: pH 7.5
assay_ionic_conditions: 10 mM Tris-HCl, 2 mM MgCl2; the authors note this buffer 'had a very low ionic strength'
assay_supercoiling: native negative supercoiling of the plasmid (supercoiled DNA, monomeric state confirmed against linearized plasmid on agarose/EtBr gels); no sigma values reported
source: PMID 38381906 (PMC11077069), Materials and methods section 'Chemical probing' and the Figure 2 legend; this primary study was identified as reference 300 of the review PMID 39723156 (PMC11667243), CANVAS section
evidence_quote: 2 ug of the repeat-containing pJH2 or pJH9 plasmid (0.424 pmol) was incubated in a 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 2 mM MgCl 2 buffer with either 6 mM KMnO 4 or the same volume of water for 2 min at 37 degrees C.
notes: Conditions taken from the primary study the review cites: Hisey et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Res 52:4361-4374, PMID 38381906 / PMC11077069. Exact length match, the probed construct is (A2G3)10, i.e. (AAGGG)10. Two caveats: (1) the review's text says 'pathogenic (AAGGG)60 repeats form H-DNA in vitro' but the chemical probing in the primary paper was done on the 10-unit repeat; (2) the structure identified is H-r3, a purine-motif (pyrimidine-purine-purine) triplex, not the classic Py*Pu*Py H-y form. Multiple conditions tested: Mg2+ gave stall patterns suggestive of triplex, K+ of G-quadruplex. Plasmid-bearing E. coli were grown at 23 C to limit repeat instability.

name: XDP_CCCTCT10
label: forming
assay_method: not reported
assay_dna_context: not reported
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: not reported
source: PMID 39723156 (PMC11667243), 'XDP' section; the review's disease table lists 'Evidence for H-DNA formation' for the XDP (CCCTCT)n motif as 'Unknown within context of this disease'
evidence_quote: no in vitro or in vivo data exist yet regarding the repeat's ability to form alternative secondary structures. Given the repeat is a hPu/hPy mirror repeat, it may form an H-DNA triplex.
notes: No primary study exists to extract conditions from: the review cites none for XDP (CCCTCT)n H-DNA and states outright that no in vitro or in vivo structural data exist; its claim is an inference from the motif being a homopurine/homopyrimidine mirror repeat. The review's only structural citation here is reference 268 (Bragg et al. 2017 PNAS, PMID 29229810), a repeat-length / age-of-onset genetics paper whose structural content is an in silico G4-DNA prediction, not an H-DNA assay. The 'forming' label for this record is therefore not backed by any assay in the cited literature and should be reconsidered.

name: CTC20_mouse
label: forming
assay_method: S1-seq in mouse cells (direct digestion of genomic DNA with the ssDNA-specific nuclease S1, ligation of biotinylated adaptors to the blunted ends, deep sequencing, mapped to mm10)
assay_dna_context: genomic DNA in cells embedded in agarose plugs and deproteinized with SDS and proteinase K; mouse testis cells (C57BL/6J and Spo11-/-) and cultured primary splenic B cells
assay_ph: pH 4.5 (nuclease S1 digestion buffer)
assay_ionic_conditions: 4.5 mM Zn2+ in the nuclease S1 digestion buffer; no other salt concentrations reported (the in-plug S1 step is cited to prior protocols)
assay_supercoiling: not directly measured; the authors propose that removing histones and other proteins while the DNA was constrained in agarose provided sufficient negative superhelicity
source: PMID 35503911 (PMC9171763), Results section 'S1-seq Patterns May Reflect Properties of Specific H-DNA Isomers', Discussion, and Methods section 'S1-seq'
evidence_quote: Relevant to these points, our nuclease S1 digestion buffer is acidic (pH 4.5) and contains 4.5 mM Zn 2+ .
notes: Matched at motif-class level: the study analysed naturally occurring mouse genomic C(TC)n repeats binned by length, with heat maps shown for n = 20, 26 and 30, so a 40 nt (CT)n tract corresponds to C(TC)20. These are endogenous genomic motifs, not a synthetic construct. Key caveat the authors state themselves: 'It is currently unclear whether the H-DNA detected formed in vitro or was already present in vivo', and they argue most or all of the triplexes may have formed ex vivo during plug processing. Temperature of the S1 digestion is not stated in this paper (method cited to refs 35, 36).

name: AG11_model
assay_method: In vitro DNA polymerase error-frequency measurement (HSV-tk forward mutation assay) with purified DNA polymerase beta on a [TC/AG]11 microsatellite template; no direct structural probing of H-DNA was performed
assay_dna_context: DNA template with the microsatellite inserted in-frame into the 5' region of the herpes simplex virus thymidine kinase (HSV-tk) gene (in vitro DNA synthesis reaction)
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: not reported
source: PMID 12173936, abstract (Eckert, Mowery & Hile 2002, Biochemistry 41:10490-8) - the primary study cited as reference 130 by the review PMID 18331847 (section 6.1) for polymerase inaccuracy at a template AG11
evidence_quote: we have determined the in vitro polymerase error frequencies at microsatellite sequences representative of those found in the human genome: [GT/CA](10), [TC/AG](11), and [TTCC/AAGG](9).
notes: The review PMID 18331847 attributes a ~4-fold decrease of polymerase accuracy at a template AG11 to this study (its reference 130) and suggests H-DNA at the repeat causes polymerase dissociation/re-association; the primary paper itself reports only error frequencies and attributes them to strand slippage, and its abstract gives no pH, temperature, salt or supercoiling. Full text is behind the ACS paywall (DOI 10.1021/bi025918c, not open access, not in PMC/Europe PMC), so no Methods conditions could be read. A companion study, Hile & Eckert 2004 (PMID 14687571, review reference 131), is the one that actually reports a triplex-attributed polymerase arrest condition: 'We detected strong polymerase pauses within the [TC](20) allele at low reaction pH which were eliminated by the addition of deaza-dGTP, consistent with these specific pauses being a consequence of triplex DNA formation during DNA synthesis.' - but that is a [TC]20 allele, not (AG)11, and no numeric pH is given in its abstract either (Elsevier full text also inaccessible). Curator should decide which primary this (AG)11 record should point to.

name: GA20_SV40
assay_method: In vivo replication-fork pause mapping: pulse labeling of SV40-variant-infected cells with [3H]thymidine and measurement of the rate of label incorporation into different regions of the SV40 genome; plus plaque morphology/titer and mixed-infection growth assays
assay_dna_context: (dG-dA)27.(dT-dC)27 tract with flanking rat sequence (200 bp total) cloned between the HpaII and KpnI sites of the SV40 genome and replicating as virus in African Green monkey kidney (CV1) cells; closed superhelical SV40 DNA (component I) isolated on CsCl gradients
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: native (in vivo) SV40 closed circular superhelical DNA; no superhelical density reported
source: PMID 2843810, abstract and Materials and Methods ('Growth of cells', 'Construction of variant SV40', 'Pulse labeling experiments') - Rao, Manor & Martin 1988, Nucleic Acids Res 16:8077-8094, the primary study cited as reference 133 by the review PMID 18331847 (section 6.1)
evidence_quote: Pulse labeling experiments indicated that the unusual inserted sequence acts as a pause site for fork progression during DNA replication, as evidenced by the rate of incorporation of radioactively labeled nucleotides into various regions of the SV40 genome.
notes: Full text of the primary study was read (OUP PDF). Two caveats for the curator: (1) the construct is (dG-dA)27.(dT-dC)27 (54 bp of alternating GA), not (GA)20 - the review PMID 18331847 labels it 'GA(20)'; (2) this paper contains no in vitro H-DNA/triplex assay at all - no pH titration, no salt series, no chemical probing, no S1/P1 nuclease - it only states that the sequence 'is known to adopt an unusual conformation that differs from both the B-form and the Z-form of DNA'. Hence pH/temperature/ionic conditions are genuinely absent rather than merely unquoted. Cells were maintained in Dulbecco Vogt Modified Eagle's medium with 5% fetal bovine serum and antibiotics (no temperature stated); the inferred fork pause was 'about one minute'. The follow-up study Rao 1994 (PMID 8144031, review reference 134) analysed the same SV40 variants' in vivo replicative intermediates by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis and describes the tracts as ones 'that can potentially adopt triplex structures'.

name: PKD1_PyRE_CT44
assay_method: P1 nuclease sensitivity and P1 cleavage-site mapping with restriction digests; two-dimensional agarose gel electrophoresis of plasmid topoisomers
assay_dna_context: Negatively supercoiled plasmid pCW31 (3.1 kb Sau3A PKD1 fragment containing the entire 2.5 kb intron 21 polypurine.polypyrimidine tract, cloned in pBluescript); relaxed and EcoRI-linearized controls
assay_ph: P1 nuclease at pH 4.6, 6.0 and 7.6 (cutting only at pH 4.6, minimal at pH 6.0, none at pH 7.6), after a 60 min preincubation at the designated pH; two-dimensional gels run at pH 7.0 and 6.0 (first dimension pH adjusted from 8.0 down to 5.0 with glacial acetic acid)
assay_temperature: P1 nuclease digestion at room temperature for 1 min; two-dimensional gel samples incubated 60 min at 37 C, then electrophoresed at 4 C at 5 V/cm for 17 h
assay_ionic_conditions: P1 reactions: 10 mM sodium acetate (pH 4.6) or 10 mM Tris (pH 6.0 or 7.6), 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2. Two-dimensional gels: 13.5 mM Tris (pH adjusted 8.0 to 5.0 with glacial acetic acid), with or without 1 mM magnesium acetate; second dimension 40 mM Tris, 25 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.3 plus 20 ug/ml chloroquine phosphate
assay_supercoiling: Native negative supercoiling (sigma = -0.05) plus topoisomer series from sigma = 0 to -0.05 and fine-mapping sets from sigma = -0.0045 to -0.0228; pCW31 transition at pH 6.0 began at topoisomer -14 (sigma = -0.024); topoisomerase-relaxed or EcoRI-linearized DNA gave no P1 cutting
source: PMID 10373576, Materials and Methods ('Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis', 'P1 nuclease reactions'), Results ('Structural transition(s) within the 2500 bp Pu.Py tract', 'Mapping P1 nuclease-sensitive sites'), Discussion, Table 1 and Fig. 3/4 legends
evidence_quote: Plasmids were incubated for 60 min at the designated pH to promote structural transitions and then digested with P1 nuclease at room temperature in 50 mM NaCl and 10 mM MgCl2 to cleave regions of single-stranded DNA.
notes: Conditions are high-confidence but the construct identity is not. This paper assays only two cloned constructs: pCW31 (entire intron 21) and pCW2966 (the 46 bp perfect mirror repeat, see HDNA0079). No 44-nucleotide CT tract was cloned or probed on its own. A 44 bp element appears only inside P1-sensitive region 2 of supercoiled pCW31: 'Region 2 contains a 57 bp imperfect mirror repeat with two overlapping 36 and 44 bp mirror repeats.' The conditions above are therefore those under which region 2 was shown to be P1-hypersensitive within the whole-intron-21 plasmid, not conditions for an isolated 44-nt construct. Note also that the paper reports a structural transition at pH 6.0 by two-dimensional gel that was not seen by P1 nuclease, attributed to the P1 buffer's 10-fold higher Mg2+ and added NaCl suppressing the transition. Curator should verify the record's 'PyRE_CT44' sequence assignment against this paper.

name: GA16_sea_urchin_histone
assay_method: Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis of plasmid topoisomers; S1 nuclease hypersensitivity
assay_dna_context: Negatively supercoiled plasmids carrying homopurine-homopyrimidine inserts
assay_ph: not reported
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: Negative supercoiling (transition described as superhelix-induced); no superhelical density reported
source: PMID 2825028, abstract
evidence_quote: Regular homopurine-homopyrimidine tracts, (dG-dA)n(dT-dC)n and (dG)n(dC)n, undergo a superhelix-induced, strongly pH-dependent, structural transition into a novel DNA conformation, the H form.
notes: Nature 1987 is not open access (Unpaywall is_oa false for 10.1038/330495a0) and the article is not in PMC or Europe PMC, so only the abstract could be read; the abstract states the transition is 'strongly pH-dependent' but gives no pH value, temperature, salt or sigma. Construct mismatch to flag: the constructs actually tested in this abstract are a tailored plasmid series carrying AAGGGAGAAXGGGGTATAGGGGYAAGAGGGAA inserts (X, Y = A or G), analysed by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis; H-form transitions were facile for X = Y = G or X = Y = A and difficult or impossible for the two non-palindromes. Neither a (GA)16 insert nor a sea urchin histone gene is mentioned anywhere in the abstract - (dG-dA)n.(dT-dC)n tracts are cited only as sequences already known to form the H form. The abstract also states 'the H form is the structural basis for S1-nuclease hypersensitivity'. Curator should verify the (GA)16 / sea-urchin-histone attribution against the full text.

name: GAAA10_human
label: forming
assay_method: S1-END-seq in human cells (ssDNA-specific S1 nuclease treatment of cells in agarose plugs converting ssDNA to DSBs, followed by END-seq); a P1-END-seq variant at neutral pH was run as a control
assay_dna_context: genomic DNA in cells embedded in 1% agarose plugs and deproteinized; human cell lines, including colon cancer lines KM12, SW48, RKO, SW620 and SW837 (Figure 3A), iPS cells (WTC11), RPE-hTERT TP53KO, and FRDA patient and sibling lymphoblasts (GM15850/GM15851)
assay_ph: pH 4.5 (S1 nuclease buffer); the P1-END-seq control used NEB1.1 buffer at pH 7
assay_temperature: 37 C for 30 min (nuclease step); preceding proteinase K step 1 h at 50 C then 7 h at 37 C
assay_ionic_conditions: 40 mM sodium acetate, 300 mM NaCl, 2 mM ZnSO4 (plus 200 U S1 nuclease per plug)
assay_supercoiling: in vivo chromatin, no defined supercoiling; the authors note the protocol 'relies on DNA dechromatinization, which creates negative DNA supercoiling'
source: PMID 36075220 (PMC9547894), STAR Methods section 'END-seq, S1-END-seq and P1-END-seq'; motif-class ranking in Results (Figure S3D) and Figure 3A legend
evidence_quote: equilibrated with two washes of S1 nuclease buffer (40 mM sodium acetate pH 4.5, 300 mM NaCl, 2 mM ZnSO4). Each wash lasted 15 minutes. We added 200 U of S1 nuclease (ThermoFisher) to 100 ul S1 nuclease buffer per plug and incubated at 37 degrees C for 30 min
notes: Matched at motif-class level to endogenous genomic repeats, not to a synthetic (GAAA)10 construct. (GAAA)n was the top-ranked class: 'Among all H-motifs, (GAAA) n /(TTTC) n were most sensitive to S1 cleavage, both in terms of the absolute abundance of S1-END-seq peaks at these repeats, as well as relative to the total number of repeats within each hPu/hPy class'. S1-sensitive sites averaged 202 bp, so the detected motifs are much longer than a 10-unit tract. Multiple conditions tested: S1-END-seq at pH 4.5 and P1-END-seq at pH 7 gave overlapping peaks, which the authors use to argue the triplexes are not an artifact of acidic pH; the (GAA)n-binding polyamide PA1 had only minimal effect on (GAAA)n peaks.

name: GGAA10_human
label: forming
assay_method: S1-END-seq in human cells (ssDNA-specific S1 nuclease treatment of cells in agarose plugs converting ssDNA to DSBs, followed by END-seq); a P1-END-seq variant at neutral pH was run as a control
assay_dna_context: genomic DNA in cells embedded in 1% agarose plugs and deproteinized; human cell lines, including colon cancer lines KM12, SW48, RKO, SW620 and SW837, iPS cells (WTC11), RPE-hTERT TP53KO, and FRDA patient and sibling lymphoblasts (GM15850/GM15851)
assay_ph: pH 4.5 (S1 nuclease buffer); the P1-END-seq control used NEB1.1 buffer at pH 7
assay_temperature: 37 C for 30 min (nuclease step); preceding proteinase K step 1 h at 50 C then 7 h at 37 C
assay_ionic_conditions: 40 mM sodium acetate, 300 mM NaCl, 2 mM ZnSO4 (plus 200 U S1 nuclease per plug)
assay_supercoiling: in vivo chromatin, no defined supercoiling; the authors note the protocol 'relies on DNA dechromatinization, which creates negative DNA supercoiling'
source: PMID 36075220 (PMC9547894), STAR Methods section 'END-seq, S1-END-seq and P1-END-seq'; motif-class ranking in Results (Figure S3D)
evidence_quote: equilibrated with two washes of S1 nuclease buffer (40 mM sodium acetate pH 4.5, 300 mM NaCl, 2 mM ZnSO4). Each wash lasted 15 minutes. We added 200 U of S1 nuclease (ThermoFisher) to 100 ul S1 nuclease buffer per plug and incubated at 37 degrees C for 30 min
notes: Matched at motif-class level to endogenous genomic repeats, not to a synthetic (GGAA)10 construct. (GGAA)n ranked second for S1 sensitivity: '(GAAA) n /(TTTC) n were most sensitive to S1 cleavage ... followed by (GGAA) n /(TTCC) n and (GAA) n /(TTC) n'. S1-sensitive sites averaged 202 bp, much longer than a 10-unit tract, and tended to have fewer sequence interruptions. Multiple conditions tested: S1-END-seq at pH 4.5 and P1-END-seq at pH 7 gave overlapping peaks; PA1 polyamide had only minimal effect on (GGAA)n peaks.

name: SV40_GACT22
assay_method: Chemical probing (OsO4 and DEPC modification) and S1 nuclease sensitivity
assay_dna_context: Supercoiled plasmid carrying the d(GA.CT)22 sequence cloned into SV40
assay_ph: Neutral pH for *H-DNA formation (base protonation not required under the zinc condition); no numeric value reported
assay_ionic_conditions: Approximately 0.4 mM ZnCl2 (zinc ions) - *H-DNA is induced by zinc at neutral pH
assay_supercoiling: Negative supercoiling facilitates formation; no superhelical density reported
source: PMID 2792082, abstract
evidence_quote: Formation of *H-DNA is facilitated by negative supercoiling and does not appear to require base protonation, since it is induced at neutral pH by approximately 0.4 mM ZnCl2.
notes: The structure demonstrated under the quoted conditions is *H-DNA, which the authors state 'differs from either B-DNA or H-DNA'; the OsO4 and DEPC patterns in zinc are 'compatible with a homopurine--homopurine--homopyridimine triplex' (Pu.Pu.Py), with other models possible. Classical H-DNA at this sequence is treated in the paper as part of a B/H/*H equilibrium, and the S1-hypersensitivity of d(GA.CT)22 is reinterpreted in terms of that equilibrium - so if this record is meant to represent canonical (pH-dependent) H-DNA rather than *H-DNA, the zinc/neutral-pH condition is the wrong one. Full text could not be read: the PMC deposit (PMC401097) is a scanned image behind a download challenge, Europe PMC fullTextXML returns HTTP 500, and the Springer/EMBO Press routes required authentication.

name: TC17_Glover
assay_method: Separation of individual H DNA conformers by agarose gel electrophoresis of topoisomers, followed by chemical probing with potassium permanganate and by acid-induced depurination mapping
assay_dna_context: Negatively supercoiled plasmid carrying a d(TC)17.d(GA)17 insert
assay_ph: not reported (stated only as 'low pH')
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: Negative superhelical stress; conformer stabilities compared at 'low negative superhelix densities' versus increasing superhelix density; no numeric sigma reported
source: PMID 2271699, abstract
evidence_quote: Polypyrimidine/polypurine DNA sequences in plasmids can adopt protonated triplex-containing structures (H DNA) in response to negative superhelical stress and low pH. A d(TC)17-d(GA)17 insert adopts two isomeric protonated structures
notes: Biochemistry 1990 is not open access (Unpaywall is_oa false for 10.1021/bi00502a014) and is not in PMC or Europe PMC, so only the abstract could be read; no numeric pH, temperature, salt or sigma is available. The abstract identifies two isomers: H-y5, in which 'the 5'-half of the d(GA)n strand participates in a triplex', and H-y3, in which 'the 3'-half forms the triplex'. H-y5 is the more stable form at low negative superhelix densities and becomes relatively less stable as superhelix density rises, and its pyrimidine foldback is less permanganate-reactive. Both forms were demonstrated, so a curator must choose which conformer this record represents.

name: TTCCC20_avian
assay_method: Oligonucleotide gel-shift (gel retardation) triplex assay, intramolecular footprinting with the single-strand-specific nucleases S1 and P1, and triplex-mediated oligonucleotide protection assays in vitro and in vivo (HeLa cells)
assay_dna_context: 287 bp quail genomic fragment containing the (TTCCC)48 mirror repeat subcloned between the XhoI and HindIII sites of an M13mp12-derived plasmid; supercoiled, relaxed and linearized plasmid and the eluted 287 bp insert all formed triplex; for the in vivo assay, plasmid plus labelled oligonucleotide electroporated into HeLa cells
assay_ph: Gel shift at pH 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 (buffers at pH 5 and 6 of 0.1 M Na-acetate; pH 7 and 8 of 0.1 M Tris-acetate). Footprinting: S1 buffer pH 4.5, P1 buffer pH 7.6
assay_temperature: 37 C throughout: 15 min incubation for gel shift and for footprinting preincubation, 10 min nuclease digestion, 5 min preincubation plus 20 min digestion for the in vitro protection assay; in vivo cells grown 24 h after electroporation
assay_ionic_conditions: Gel shift: with or without 10 mM MgCl2, in 0.1 M Na-acetate (pH 5, 6) or 0.1 M Tris-acetate (pH 7, 8). S1 buffer: 50 mM NaOAc pH 4.5, 200 mM NaCl, 1 mM ZnCl2, 1% glycerol. P1 buffer: 10 mM Tris-Cl pH 7.6, 50 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl2, 1 mM dithiothreitol
assay_supercoiling: Not required - both supercoiled (I) and relaxed (II) plasmid forms retained oligonucleotides, and linearized plasmid and the isolated 287 bp insert gave the same result
source: PMID 1741277, Materials and Methods ('Gel shift experiments', 'Intramolecular footprinting of triplex structures', 'Triplex-mediated oligonucleotide protection in vitro / in vivo'), Results, Discussion, and Fig. 2, 3 and 4 legends
evidence_quote: Extreme conditions (pH: 5.0, no MgCl2) and (pH: 8.0, 10 mM MgCl2) lead respectively to the formation of PU-PY-PY and PU-PU-PY structures.
notes: Full text read from the OUP scan (embedded OCR text layer). Multiple conditions: the pyrimidine-motif (PU-PY-PY) triplex forms at pH 5.0 without Mg2+, the purine-motif (PU-PU-PY) triplex at pH 8.0 with 10 mM MgCl2, and both coexist at all intermediate pH/Mg2+ combinations - 'low pH and Mg2+ have opposite effects in displacing an equilibrium between these alternative structures.' The S1 and P1 buffers were chosen because they match the PU-PY-PY and PU-PU-PY conditions respectively; in both conformers the single-stranded half is the 5' half of the repeat. The biologically relevant (in vivo) form is PU-PU-PY. Explicit negative result on supercoiling: 'figure 2 shows that supercoiling is not required for triplex formation of this long mirror repeat.' Construct mismatch to flag: the repeat is (TTCCC)48 (60% G+C, promoter of the quail T64 gene), not (TTCCC)20 as the record name suggests.

name: gamma_globin_228_189
assay_method: S1 nuclease sensitivity of supercoiled plasmids (asymmetric cleavage) plus direct mapping by Watson-Crick hybridization of exogenous oligomers to the single-stranded region; in PMID 8188694 the same supercoiled-plasmid structure is used as a protein-binding substrate and probed by HPFH point mutations
assay_dna_context: Negatively supercoiled plasmid containing the human gamma-globin -228 to -189 homopyrimidine-homopurine region
assay_ph: Acidic / low pH (no numeric value reported in the abstracts that could be read)
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported
assay_supercoiling: Negative supercoiling of plasmid DNA; no superhelical density reported
source: PMID 8188694, abstract (states the -228/-189 region forms H-DNA in supercoiled plasmids); the conditions themselves come from the primary study it refers back to, PMID 1382059 (Ulrich, Gray & Ley 1992, J Biol Chem 267:18649), abstract
evidence_quote: this structure is formed in a homopyrimidine-homopurine tract and is stabilized by acidic pH and negative supercoiling of plasmid DNA
notes: PMID 8188694 itself reports no structural assay conditions; it opens 'We previously determined that a region between positions -228 and -189 upstream from the human gamma-globin genes can form an intramolecular triplex (H-DNA) in supercoiled plasmids' and shows that the high-affinity BP-8 site in supercoiled plasmids 'is stabilized by factors that stabilize H-DNA' and is abolished by the HPFH -202 C->G and C->T mutations. The structural conditions above are from the cited primary study PMID 1382059, which also reports that the structure 'is asymmetrically cleaved by S1 nuclease' and so 'probably contains a single-stranded region and an intramolecular triplex'. Neither JBC paper is in PMC or Europe PMC and both are Elsevier-hosted (jbc.org and sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403), so no Methods-level pH, temperature or salt values could be read. For a fuller condition set on the same region a curator can use Bacolla et al. 1995 (PMID 7592674), which probed it with osmium tetroxide, chloroacetaldehyde and diethyl pyrocarbonate and reports unpaired nucleotides at -209 through -217 with 'These reactivities were induced by negative supercoiling, low pH, and magnesium ions.'

name: PKD1_46bp_mirror
assay_method: Two-dimensional agarose gel electrophoresis of plasmid topoisomers combined with chemical probing (KMnO4 and chloroacetaldehyde) read out by primer extension; supported by P1 nuclease sensitivity
assay_dna_context: Negatively supercoiled plasmid pCW2966 (46 bp perfect PKD1 intron 21 mirror repeat, CCTCCTCCTCCCCCTCCTCCCTCCTCCCTCCTCCCCCTCCTCCTCC, bp 34613-34658, cloned into the EcoRI site of pUC19); pUC19 without the insert as control
assay_ph: pH 5.0 (structural transition present at pH 5.0, absent at pH 7.0); chemical modification in 50 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA at pH 5.0
assay_temperature: 1 h incubation at 37 C before chemical treatment; chemical treatment at room temperature (KMnO4 5 min, chloroacetaldehyde 2.5 h); two-dimensional gel samples incubated 60 min at 37 C then run at 4 C at 5 V/cm for 17 h
assay_ionic_conditions: Chemical probing: 50 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA (pH 5.0), with 20 mM KMnO4 or 50% chloroacetaldehyde added. Two-dimensional gels: 13.5 mM Tris with 1 mM MgCl2 (Fig. 1 legend) / 13.5 mM Tris with or without 1 mM magnesium acetate (Methods); second dimension 40 mM Tris, 25 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.3 plus 20 ug/ml chloroquine phosphate
assay_supercoiling: Average superhelical density sigma = -0.05 for the chemical probing; in two-dimensional gels the transition occurred at topoisomer -9, corresponding to sigma = -0.0375, and removed about 4.8 superhelical turns
source: PMID 10373576, Materials and Methods ('Chemical modification', 'Generation of plasmid topoisomers', 'Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis'), Results ('A mirror repeat region from intron 21 forms an H-y3 intramolecular triplex DNA'), Discussion, and Fig. 1, 2 and 5 legends
evidence_quote: each sample containing 1 µg of supercoiled pCW2966, at an average superhelical density of σ = –0.05 was incubated in 40 µl of 50 mM sodium acetate, 1 mM EDTA (pH 5.0). After a 1 h incubation at 37°C, samples were treated with chemicals at room temperature
notes: This is the construct for which H-DNA was actually demonstrated in this paper: an H-y3 intramolecular triplex (3'-half of the pyrimidine strand in Hoogsteen pairing, C+.G.C triplets). Specificity controls: 'Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis of pCW2966 topoisomers demonstrated a transition at pH 5.0 that was absent at pH 7.0' and 'No transitions were observed at pH 5.0 in the parent plasmid, pUC19'. KMnO4 marks unpaired thymines, chloroacetaldehyde unpaired A/C (and weakly G); modified positions map to a single-stranded loop (T22) and the triplex-duplex boundary (T49/T50, A47/A48/A52, C51) plus unpaired adenines across positions 23-50 of the purine strand. The 46 bp repeat lies within the 55 bp mirror repeat of P1-sensitive region 4, the strongest P1 site in pCW31. The authors also note they had to add betaine, DMSO and a helper oligonucleotide to let polymerases traverse the repeat, i.e. triplex formed even at neutral pH and high PCR temperature in that context.

name: Hanvey1988_(TTC)8
label: forming
assay_method: enzymatic probing with S1 and P1 nucleases and chemical probing with bromoacetaldehyde, OsO4, diethyl pyrocarbonate and dimethyl sulfate, resolved at base-pair level; plus supercoil-induced relaxation studies using two-dimensional gels
assay_dna_context: recombinant plasmid harbouring the synthetic (TTC)8.(GAA)8 insert in the pRW790 vector (supercoiled plasmid)
assay_ph: 4.5-5.0 (stabilizing but not required; probing was carried out across a range of pH values that the abstract does not enumerate)
assay_ionic_conditions: not reported (ionic strength was varied with NaCl, but no concentrations are given in the abstract)
assay_supercoiling: negative supercoiling (the non-B conformation "is stabilized by negative supercoiling"); no sigma value reported
source: PMID 2835375, abstract
evidence_quote: "The specific reactions at the base pair level of these inserts with enzymatic (S1 and P1 nucleases) and chemical (bromoacetaldehyde, OsO4, diethyl pyrocarbonate, and dimethyl sulfate) probes were evaluated as influenced by pH, negative supercoiling, and ionic strength (NaCl)."
notes: Full text could not be obtained: no PMC deposit, and jbc.org (both /fulltext and /pdf for S0021-9258(18)68654-5) and sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403, so only the abstract was read. (TTC)8.(GAA)8 is the 33% G+C insert, one of the "five inserts with 66-25% G+C" that the abstract concludes "adopt a non-B right-handed conformation which is stabilized by negative supercoiling", best explained by "An intramolecular triple-stranded model". The abstract states "Low pH (pH values 4.5-5.0) tends to stabilize this structure but is not essential for its formation", so H-DNA does not strictly require acidic pH here. Temperature, buffer and NaCl concentrations are in the unread Methods. A free companion paper from the same group (Hanvey, Shimizu & Wells 1988 PNAS, PMC281955, 'Intramolecular DNA triplexes in supercoiled plasmids') may carry comparable conditions but covers different inserts and was not read.
